title: Consultant - Digital and AI Safety for Women Entrepreneurs
description:
Result of Service

The consultant shall commit to performing the tasks stated above with high integrity and dedication to delivering the outputs as per plan. He/she shall be professionally accountable to Economic Affairs Officer, SRO-SSWA. Within the overall parameters set out in this agreement, the Consultant will work according to the agreed ToR.

Work Location

Remotely

Expected duration

5.5 months

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Economic Affairs Officer responsible for the women’s entrepreneurship programme at SRO-SSWA, the consultant will develop practical training materials, prepare policy recommendations and deliver training on the safe use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI). The assignment will begin with women entrepreneurs in India. Its core materials will be designed for later adaptation across South Asia. The consultant will undertake the following tasks: 1. Review programme materials and consult women entrepreneurs, trainers and relevant institutions to identify priority safety risks in everyday business use of digital platforms, e-commerce, digital payments and AI tools. 2. Develop and test a plain-language training manual that helps women use these tools to promote their businesses while protecting their money, business information, personal safety and families. 3. Prepare evidence-based policy recommendations for a safer and more inclusive digital and AI environment for women entrepreneurs, drawing on the India pilot and selected South Asian experience. 4. Deliver practical workshop sessions, introduce the manual to participants and trainers, and revise the materials using feedback and learning assessments. 5. Submit all agreed outputs, source files and supporting evidence to the Economic Affairs Officer in charge of the women’s entrepreneurship programme at SRO-SSWA. The following are the activities and engagements for the consultant: All month references are measured from the contract start date. The scope below provides for three training engagements: two workshops in India and one regional session. Workshop dates and formats will be confirmed in the inception plan. Output 1 Inception report By the end of Month 1, submit an inception report of approximately 6–8 pages, excluding annexes, to outline the proposed methodology and analysis. The inception report should include a review of relevant literature available from ESCAP, UN and governments and other institutions in India and South Asia and a list of government institutions and women entrepreneurs in India and representatives of training partners, women’s business networks and relevant digital safety institutions to consult in the needs assessment. Output 2 Needs assessment and Draft training manual and teaching materials Undertake consultations with identified stakeholders to understand the needs of women entrepreneurs and the eco-system of institutions and partners and their potential roles in the support process. The needs assessment report will set out priority learning needs, common business risks, the manual outline, consultation findings, proposed learning assessments and a workplan. It will identify two additional South Asian countries for a focused desk review, selected with ESCAP, and explain which elements require country-specific adaptation. By the end of Month 3, submit a complete draft manual in English, normally 30–40 pages excluding annexes, with a companion slide deck and facilitator notes. Keep modules short, illustrated and suitable for smartphone reading and low-cost printing. Provide step-by-step actions, realistic business examples, checklists, practice exercises and a brief glossary. Avoid technical language and explain essential terms when first used. The manual will cover the following content: • Safe business use of AI: drafting product descriptions, marketing content, translations and customer messages; checking facts and outputs; protecting customer and business information; recognising bias and misleading content; and respecting consent and intellectual property. • Account and device protection: strong passwords or passkeys, multi-factor authentication, recovery options, updates, backups, app permissions and safer use of shared devices. Explain how to separate business and family information where possible. • Safer e-commerce and payments: checking buyers, suppliers and platform messages; recognising fake orders, payment screenshots, refund requests, phishing links, QR-code and UPI fraud; and using official payment and platform support channels. • AI-enabled deception and personal safety: impersonation, cloned voices, deepfake images or videos, fake AI services, harassment and threats involving family members. Teach independent verification and safe reporting rather than relying on visual clues alone. • Responding to an incident: stopping further payments or disclosure, contacting the bank or payment provider promptly, securing accounts, preserving evidence safely and using verified reporting channels. Include a short action card and explain that reporting does not guarantee recovery of funds. Use fictional data and safe demonstrations. Do not request passwords, one-time passcodes, live bank details or sensitive customer records. Include India-specific official reporting guidance in a clearly marked annex, with verification dates. Provide a reusable country annex structure so that Indian procedures are not presented as regional rules. Output 3 Tested manual and finalized training package By the end of Month 4, test the draft with women entrepreneurs with varied levels of digital experience and trainers. Participants may include people consulted for Output 1. Use practical scenarios to check whether participants can recognise risks and follow protective steps. Submit anonymised findings, a summary of changes and a response to ESCAP’s comments. Deliver the revised manual, participant checklists, incident action card, facilitator notes, slides and short pre- and post-session assessments. Include at least one exercise per module and guidance on local-language delivery and accessibility. Translation is outside the proposed scope; editable files must support later translation. ESCAP’s acceptance will depend on accuracy, usability, completeness and incorporation of agreed revisions. Output 4 Policy recommendations for a safer digital and AI environment By the end of Month 5, submit a policy paper of approximately 12–15 pages, excluding references, and a two-page policy brief. Draw on consultations, the India pilot and the focused desk review of two additional South Asian countries. Distinguish findings supported by evidence from issues requiring further investigation. Do not generalise India’s experience to the whole subregion. Assess gaps in prevention, accessible reporting, redress and institutional support. Address data protection, AI-enabled fraud, online harassment, platform and payment-provider responsibilities, digital literacy and support for small and informal women-led businesses. Verify relevant laws and policies against official sources and distinguish measures in force from proposals or measures awaiting implementation. Present a practical action matrix identifying each recommendation, its evidence base, proposed lead institution, partners, priority, indicative resource needs and progress indicator. Separate near-term operational measures from longer-term policy options. Identify opportunities for regional peer learning. Recommendations should support safe participation and avoid unnecessary costs or barriers for women-led enterprises. Incorporate ESCAP’s comments before final submission. Output 5 Training delivery and workshop reports Deliver two workshops in India and one regional session. Plan for at least three hours of facilitated teaching and exercises at each India workshop and a 90-minute regional session. ESCAP will arrange participants, venues, connectivity and local-language support, as required. The regional session will present lessons from India and explain how to adapt the materials. Tailor each session to the participants’ business activities and digital confidence. Introduce and share the manual, demonstrate safe routines and help local trainers reuse the materials. Submit a short report within ten working days of each engagement, including the agenda, materials used, assessment results and recommended changes. Report learning results with their limitations; do not attribute changes in income or fraud losses to a short training session. Output 6 Final package and handover By the end of the consultancy, submit the final manual and teaching materials updated after the workshops, the final policy paper and brief, and a short completion report. Provide an adaptation guide covering language, payment systems, relevant laws, reporting channels and referral services. Include a dated source register and instructions for updating information that may change. Supply editable Word and PowerPoint source files, accessible PDFs and any original illustrations or other assets needed for reuse. All outputs must contain clear references, respect third-party rights and be ready for ESCAP review and subsequent publication clearance. ESCAP will provide consolidated comments. The consultant will submit revisions based on the received comments. The inception plan will allow for these review periods. Changes to deliverables, fees or the contract end date require written agreement under applicable contract procedures. Workshop rescheduling will be addressed promptly through an agreed revised schedule.

Qualifications/special skills

An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, digital policy or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in a relevant field, combined with two additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible professional experience in cybersecurity, digital safety or closely related work is required.Experience preparing evidence-based policy analysis or recommendations on digital safety, cybersecurity, AI governance or a closely related field. An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, digital policy or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in a relevant field, combined with two additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. Practical experience addressing online fraud, privacy, account security and risks arising from the use or misuse of AI, including generative AI. Experience designing plain-language training materials and delivering participatory digital safety training for non-technical audiences. Experience supporting women entrepreneurs or women-led micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in the use of e-commerce, social commerce or digital payments. Professional experience in South Asia, including India, and demonstrated knowledge of the region’s digital business environment and gender-related barriers to safe digital participation. Relevant assignments in at least two South Asian countries; work with rural, home-based or informal enterprises; and experience with the UN or other international development organizations.

Languages

Fluency in English, both written and oral, is required. Working knowledge of Hindi or another South Asian language is desirable.

Additional Information

Consultancy fee: USD 20,000 (payable upon acceptance of above-mentioned deliverables) Payment schedule: •10% upon acceptance of Deliverable 1 •25% upon acceptance of Deliverable 2 •20% upon acceptance of Deliverable 3 •15% upon acceptance of Deliverable 4 •15% upon acceptance of Deliverable 5 •15% upon acceptance of final package and completed handover

No Fee

THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.

**Description**

At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd  
  
India's 11,099-kilometer coastline is home to 250 million people and supports key blue economy sectors including fisheries, tourism, agriculture, and transport. Despite its ecological richness, India's coastal ecosystems face mounting pressure from climate-induced hazards, coastal erosion, pollution, and land-use change. One-third of India's coastline is reported as vulnerable to erosion, threatening livelihoods, settlements, and biodiversity of global significance.  
  
The SHORE MPA has begun implementation in the states of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka under Phase 1 and will be expanded to other coastal states such as Goa, Maharashtra, Puducherry and West Bengal under subsequent phases. It aims to increase the resilience of targeted coastal communities and ecosystems, focusing on four components: (i) strengthening institutions for Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM); (ii) shoreline management, coastal protection and conservation; (iii) improving livelihoods for natural resource-dependent communities; and (iv) enhancing marine pollution management and plastic circularity.  
  
Nature-based solutions (NBS) are central to Component 2, which supports mangrove, seagrass and coral reef conservation management and restoration, along with shelter belts, bio-shields, and hybrid coastal erosion management measures such as beach nourishment, sand dune stabilization, artificial reefs, and others. Where relevant, NBS investments should be coordinated with livelihood activities such as eco-tourism and mangrove-friendly value chains to ensure that conservation-livelihood tradeoffs are managed. The project also involves establishment of Centers of Excellence for coastal ecosystem management, long-term biodiversity monitoring, and eco-tourism.  
  
The Environment (ENV) Department in South Asia seeks to recruit a highly skilled and motivated ET Consultant (Nature-based Solutions Specialist) to provide technical, operational, and analytical support to the World Bank task team and the state-level implementing agencies in planning, implementing, and monitoring nature-based solutions for coastal resilience under the SHORE MPA. The ET Consultant will report to the ENV Practice Manager for the South Asia Region (SAR) and work under the supervision of the SHORE Task Team Leaders.  
  
The South Asia Region comprises six countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. It was the second-fastest growing region in the world in the aftermath of the global crisis. This strong growth has translated into declining poverty and impressive improvements in human development. The percentage of people living below the poverty line fell in South Asia from 56% to 16% between 1981 and 2013. Still, the region remains home to a third of the world’s poorest, with 216 million people living below $1.9/day.  
  
The South Asia Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar

The Environment Department (ENV), located within the World Bank’s Planet Practice Group has been established to deliver on the opportunities, benefits and outcomes offered by enhanced management of the environment and natural resources. ENV provides expertise, technical assistance and financing to help countries manage land, sea and freshwater natural resources in a sustainable way to help create jobs, improve livelihoods, enhance ecosystem services, decrease pollution and increase resilience to climate change. Over 360 ENV staff working across the globe help set developing countries on a clean, green growth trajectory for resilient economies and healthy communities.  
  
The SSAE1 unit comprises around 30 staff, with 95 percent based in Country Offices. The rest of the team is based in Washington DC. Our Sri Lanka country office is a joint World Bank/International Finance Cooperation office, comprising approximately 100 staff, including an ETC working on environment, providing a vibrant, collegial working environment.  
  
**Duties and accountabilities:**  
  
The ET Consultant will have the following tasks:  
  
**1)Technical Advisory and Operational Support**  
  

* Provide technical guidance to the task team and clients on the design, siting, and implementation of NBS interventions including mangrove, coastal sandy-soil & cliff forests, seagrass and coral reef conservation and restoration, bio-shields and shelter belts, and hybrid erosion management.
* Support preparation and quality review of sub-project-level technical designs for NBS activities, including for e.g. Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and Biodiversity Management Plans (BMPs).
* Advise on screening of NBS sub-project sites to avoid ecologically sensitive areas, no-go zones, and areas with high biodiversity value in line with State Coastal Zone Management Plans (CZMP) and Shoreline Management Plans (SMP).
* Contribute to Implementation Support Missions and progress report reviews from implementing agencies related to NBS design and implementation.

  
**2)Global Knowledge and Technical Expertise**  
  

* Support the implementation of nature-based solutions-related advisory services and knowledge products, including through technical inputs, guidance materials, and planning for the timely delivery of analytical products.
* Generate and curate knowledge, such as by identifying best practices and lessons learned on NBS for coastal protection, and promote dissemination at the national and global levels.
* Support the team in technical assessments/analyses related to NBS e.g. cost-benefit analysis frameworks for NBS interventions, assessment of ecosystem services and livelihoods benefits.
* Support the design and operationalization of long-term NBS/ecosystem monitoring programs in line with project results frameworks.

  
**3)Stakeholder Engagement and Capacity Building**  
  

* Contribute to the engagement and policy dialogue with government counterparts and other collaborators in the NBS space.
* Support capacity building and knowledge sharing activities for state officials, community groups, and technical staff on NBS principles, implementation, and adaptive management. This may include knowledge exchange between SHORE state teams, with national institutions (e.g., NCSCM, NIOT, NCCR, IIT-Madras, SDMRI), and with other countries that are implementing coastal NBS projects.
* Engage with local natural-resource dependent communities and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in the design of community-driven NBS interventions.

**Selection Criteria**

* Master's (or higher) degree in marine ecology, coastal engineering, forestry, environmental science, natural resource management, geography, or a closely related field.

  

* Minimum of 8 years of relevant professional experience in nature-based solutions, forestry/mangroves, coastal ecosystem management, coastal resilience, natural resource management, and/or sustainable development fields with demonstrated experience in World Bank operations and analytics.

  

* Demonstrated knowledge and expertise on nature-based solutions, which may include mangrove restoration, coral reef rehabilitation, seagrass conservation, shelter belts, bio-shields, or green-grey hybrid coastal protection.

  

* Strong technical skills with remote sensing, coastal modeling tools, or GIS as applied to coastal ecosystem management.

  

* Strong analytical skills, ability to think strategically, analyze and synthesize diverse qualitative and quantitative data and information. Ability to develop, conduct, or review assessments of NBS design and implementation is an advantage.

  

* Excellent writing skills and ability to produce high-quality analytical and advisory outputs for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  

* Experience working on South Asia and familiarity with the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification framework and ICZM principles in the Indian context is an advantage.

  

* Good team player who can work as a member of a multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural team, motivate and lead group efforts and network effectively across boundaries.

  

* A drive for results while working with limited supervision and under tight timelines.

  
**Additional Considerations:**  
  
**As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who:**  

* Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries.
* Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making.
* Bring experience working on fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV)-related contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable.

description:
**Your potential, unleashed.**

  
  

India’s impact on the global economy has increased at an exponential rate and Deloitte presents an opportunity to unleash and realize your potential amongst cutting edge leaders, and organizations shaping the future of the region, and indeed, the world beyond.

  
  

At Deloitte, your whole self to work, every day. Combine that with our drive to propel with purpose and you have the perfect playground to collaborate, innovate, grow, and make an impact that matters.

  
  
  

**The team**

  
  

Deloitte helps organizations prevent cyberattacks and protect valuable assets. We believe in being secure, vigilant, and resilient—not only by looking at how to prevent and respond to attacks, but at how to manage cyber risk in a way that allows you to unleash new opportunities. Embed cyber risk at the start of strategy development for more effective management of information and technology risks

  
  
  

**Your work profile.**

  
  

As a **Consultant** in our Cyber Team, you’ll build and nurture positive working relationships with teams and clients with the intention to exceed client expectations: -

  
  

**Role Summary**

  
  

* Monitor and analyze security alerts from SIEM tools (e.g., Splunk, QRadar, Sentinel).
* Perform initial triage, prioritization, and escalation of security incidents.
* Identify false positives and escalate legitimate threats to L2.
* Maintain incident tracking and documentation using ticketing systems.
* Ensure compliance with SOC runbooks and standard operating procedures.
* Perform in-depth investigation of escalated security incidents and alerts.
* Conduct root cause analysis, correlate logs across sources, and identify the threat actor's behavior.
* Lead incident response activities and provide recommendations for containment and remediation.
* Develop and tune use cases, detection rules, and correlation logic in SIEM platforms.
* Work closely with other teams for threat containment and post-incident reporting.
* Mentor L1 analysts and support their technical development.
  

  

**Required Skills**

  
  

* Hands-on experience with SIEM platforms (e.g., Splunk, QRadar, Microsoft Sentinel).
* Familiarity with EDR tools (e.g., CrowdStrike, MS Defender, Carbon Black).
* Knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain, and incident response lifecycle.
* Strong understanding of network protocols, Windows/Linux OS logs, and threat vectors.
* Good analytical, communication, and documentation skills.
* Relevant certifications like CEH, CompTIA Security+, Splunk Power User Certified, etc., are preferred.
  

  

**Desired Qualification:**

  
  

* B.Tech/BE / B.Sc / BCA/ full time graduation / Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering/ Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, IT, Cybersecurity, or equivalent
* 5-8yrs of total experience.
* 5+ years of experience in SOC operations (L1 or L2 level).
  

  

**Location and way of working**

  
  

* Base location: Delhi
* Professional is required to work from office.
  

  

**Your role as Consultant**

We expect our people to embrace and live our purpose by challenging themselves to identify issues that are most important for our clients, our people, and for society.

  
  

In addition to living our purpose, lead across our organization must strive to be:

  
  

* Inspiring - Leading with integrity to build inclusion and motivation
* Committed to creating purpose - Creating a sense of vision and purpose
* Agile - Achieving high-quality results through collaboration and Team unity
* Skilled at building diverse capability - Developing diverse capabilities for the future
* Persuasive / Influencing - Persuading and influencing stakeholders
* Collaborating - Partnering to build new solutions
* Delivering value - Showing commercial acumen
* Committed to expanding business - Leveraging new business opportunities
* Analytical Acumen - Leveraging data to recommend impactful approach and solutions through the power of analysis and visualization
* Effective communication – Must be well abled to have well-structured and well-articulated conversations to achieve win-win possibilities
* Engagement Management / Delivery Excellence - Effectively managing engagement(s) to ensure timely and proactive execution as well as course correction for the success of engagement(s).
* Managing change - Responding to changing environment with resilience
* Managing Quality & Risk - Delivering high quality results and mitigating risks with utmost integrity and precision
* Strategic Thinking & Problem Solving - Applying strategic mindset to solve business issues and complex problems
* Tech Savvy - Leveraging ethical technology practices to deliver high impact for clients and for Deloitte
* Empathetic leadership and inclusivity - creating a safe and thriving environment where everyone's valued for who they are, use empathy to understand others to adapt our behaviours and attitudes to become more inclusive.
  

  

**How you’ll grow**

  
  

***Connect for impact***

  
  

Our exceptional team of professionals across the globe are solving some of the world’s most complex business problems, as well as directly supporting our communities, the planet, and each other. Know more in our Global Impact Report and our India Impact Report.

  
  
  

***Empower to lead***

  
  

You can be a leader irrespective of your career level. Our colleagues are characterised by their ability to inspire, support, and provide opportunities for people to deliver their best and grow both as professionals and human beings. Know more about Deloitte and our One Young World partnership.

  
  
  

***Inclusion for all***

  
  

At Deloitte, people are valued and respected for who they are and are trusted to add value to their clients, teams and communities in a way that reflects their own unique capabilities. Know more about everyday steps that you can take to be more inclusive. At Deloitte, we believe in the unique skills, attitude and potential each and every one of us brings to the table to make an impact that matters.

  
  
  

***Drive your career***

  
  

At Deloitte, you are encouraged to take ownership of your career. We recognise there is no one size fits all career path, and global, cross-business mobility and up / re-skilling are all within the range of possibilities to shape a unique and fulfilling career. Know more about Life at Deloitte.

  
  
  

**Everyone’s welcome… entrust your happiness to us**

  
  
  

Our workspaces and initiatives are geared towards your 360-degree happiness. This includes specific needs you may have in terms of accessibility, flexibility, safety and security, and caregiving. Here’s a glimpse of things that are in store for you.

  
  
  

**Interview tips**

  
  

We want job seekers exploring opportunities at Deloitte to feel prepared, confident and comfortable. To help you with your interview, we suggest that you do your research, know some background about the organisation and the business area you’re applying to. Check out recruiting tips from Deloitte professionals.

No one other than an authorized official of Deloitte is permitted to offer or confirm any job offer from Deloitte. We advise career aspirants to exercise caution.

title: Salesforce Developer, Principal
description:
As a Principal Salesforce Developer at Epicor, you will be a key technical expert responsible for designing, building, and optimizing advanced Salesforce solutions across multiple business functions. You will architect modern Lightning Web Component experiences, ensure high‑quality Apex development, and take the lead on complex projects involving Salesforce CPQ, Billing, and other critical business systems. Your work will directly influence the scalability, usability, and effectiveness of Epicor’s Salesforce ecosystem.

  

**Key responsibilities**

**Architecture and development**

* Architect and build scalable Salesforce solutions on the platform across the full Quote to Cash lifecycle: product catalog, pricing, quoting, contracts, orders, renewals, amendments, billing, invoicing and revenue recognition.
* Design and develop on Salesforce CPQ and Salesforce Billing, including price rules, product rules, QCP (Quote Calculator Plugin), advanced approvals, billing schedules, invoice runs and revenue recognition.
* Write high-quality Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flows and integrations; set the standard for code quality, performance and security.
* Own the technical design for integrations between Salesforce and ERP, payment, tax and provisioning systems using REST/SOAP APIs, Platform Events and middleware.

**Monetization and AI**

* Design monetization solutions for consumption and usage-based pricing, including usage capture, rating, commitments, overages and hybrid subscription models.
* Lead UX design for seller-facing quoting experiences that reduce clicks, errors and cycle time.
* Build AI-driven quote automation, such as guided selling, quote recommendations, deal desk assistance and agent-based workflows.

**Technical leadership**

* Act as the technical authority for Q2C on Salesforce; review designs and code, and mentor developers and admins.
* Drive DevOps best practices: source control, CI/CD, automated testing and release management.
Evaluate new Salesforce releases and features, and recommend how to apply them to GTM initiatives.  

**Required qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 12+ years in software development, with 10+ years building on the Salesforce platform.
* 7+ years of hands-on, in-depth experience with Salesforce CPQ (Steelbrick); strong working knowledge of Salesforce Billing.
* Expert in Apex, Lightning Web Components, SOQL, Flows and the Salesforce data model, including governor limits and performance tuning.
* Proven experience designing end-to-end Quote to Cash processes, including subscriptions, renewals, amendments and usage-based billing.
* Strong integration experience with REST/SOAP APIs, Platform Events and middleware such as MuleSoft, Workato or Boomi.
* Experience with Salesforce DevOps tools such as Copado, Gearset or SFDX with Git-based CI/CD.

**Preferred qualifications**

* Salesforce certifications: Application Architect or System Architect, Platform Developer II, CPQ Specialist, Billing Specialist.
* Background in consumption or usage-based pricing for SaaS or cloud businesses.
* Experience in enterprise software or ERP companies, and with global teams across time zones.
* UX design skills, such as building seller workflows from user research and prototypes.

**About Epicor**

At Epicor, we’re truly a team. Join 5,000 talented professionals in creating a world of better business through data, AI, and cognitive ERP. We help businesses stay future-ready by connecting people, processes, and technology. From software engineers who command the latest AI technology to business development reps who help us seize new opportunities, the work we do matters. Together, Epicor employees are creating a more resilient global supply chain.

**We’re** **Proactive, Proud, Partners** **.**

Whatever your career journey, we’ll help you find the right path. Through our training courses, mentorship, and continuous support, you’ll get everything you need to thrive. At Epicor, your success is our success. And that success really matters, because we’re the essential partners for the world’s most essential businesses—the hardworking companies who make, move, and sell the things the world needs.

**Competitive Pay & Benefits**

* **Health and Wellness:** Comprehensive health and wellness benefits designed to support your overall well-being.

* **Internal Mobility:** Opportunities for mentorship, continuing education, and focused career goal setting, with 25% of positions filled internally.

* **Career Development:** Free LinkedIn Learning licenses for everyone, along with our Mentoring Program to boost your personal development.

* **Education Support:** Geographically specific programs to balance the cost of education with the benefits of continued learning and personal development.

* **Inclusive Workplace:** Collaborate with a diverse team in an inclusive, global workplace that fosters innovation and celebrates partnership.

* **Work-Life Balance:** Policies built on mutual trust and support, encouraging time off to rest, recharge, and reconnect.

* **Global Mobility:** Comprehensive support for international relocations and permanent residency processes.

**Equal Opportunities and Accommodations Statement**

Epicor is committed to creating a workplace and global community where inclusion is valued; where you bring the whole and real you— that’s who we’re interested in. If you have interest in this or any role- but your experience doesn’t match every qualification of the job description, that’s okay- consider applying regardless.

We are an equal-opportunity employer.

description:

**Job #:**

req39137

**Description**

At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd  
  
India's 11,099 kilometer coastline is home to 250 million people and supports key blue economy sectors including fisheries, tourism, agriculture, and transport. Despite its ecological richness, India's coastal ecosystems face mounting pressure from climate-induced hazards, coastal erosion, pollution, and land-use change. One-third of India's coastline is reported as vulnerable to erosion, threatening livelihoods, settlements, and biodiversity of global significance.  
  
The Strengthening Coastal Resilience and the Economy (SHORE) program has begun implementation in the states of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka under Phase 1 and will be expanded to other coastal states such as Goa, Maharashtra, Puducherry and West Bengal under subsequent phases. It aims to increase the resilience of targeted coastal communities and ecosystems, focusing on four components: (i) strengthening institutions for Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM); (ii) shoreline management, coastal protection and conservation; (iii) improving livelihoods for natural resource-dependent communities; and (iv) enhancing marine pollution management and plastic circularity.  
  
**The Position:**  
  
The Environment (ENV) Department in South Asia seeks to recruit a highly skilled recruit a highly skilled and motivated Extended Term (ET) Consultant (Coastal Engineering Specialist) who would work as part of various task teams involved in preparing and providing technical assistance to World Bank-financed projects/activities involving Coastal hydrodynamic processes, coastal protection/conservation measures and cruise terminal/harbour construction and modernization.  
  
This position will be based in New Delhi, India. The candidate is expected to work across several countries in the South Asia Region. The Coastal Engineer will report to the ENV Practice Manager for the South Asia Region (SAR) and work under the supervision of the SHORE Task Team Leaders.
  
  
The South Asia Region comprises six countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. It was the second-fastest growing region in the world in the aftermath of the global crisis. This strong growth has translated into declining poverty and impressive improvements in human development. The percentage of people living below the poverty line fell in South Asia from 56% to 16% between 1981 and 2013. Still, the region remains home to a third of the world’s poorest, with 216 million people living below $1.9/day.  
  
The South Asia Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar  
  
**The Unit**  
  
The Environment Department (ENV), located within the World Bank’s Planet Practice Group has been established to deliver on the opportunities, benefits and outcomes offered by enhanced management of the environment and natural resources. ENV provides expertise, technical assistance and financing to help countries manage land, sea and freshwater natural resources in a sustainable way to help create jobs, improve livelihoods, enhance ecosystem services, decrease pollution and increase resilience to climate change. Over 360 ENV staff working across the globe help set developing countries on a clean, green growth trajectory for resilient economies and healthy communities.  
  
The SSAE1 unit comprises around 30 staff, with 95 percent based in Country Offices. The rest of the team is based in Washington DC. Our Sri Lanka country office is a joint World Bank/International Finance Cooperation office, comprising approximately 100 staff, including an ETC working on environment, providing a vibrant, collegial working environment.  
Duties and accountabilities:  
  
**The ET Consultant will have the following tasks:**  
  

* Support the Bank team by providing engineering oversight and guidance on all infrastructure interventions, technical matters relating to planning, design, and implementation of the civil works activities related to protection, rehabilitation and integrated management of coastal areas. The grey infrastructure interventions may include, but not limited to, coastal protection structures such as submerged reefs, rubble mound breakwaters, concrete sea walls, groynes, pollution treatment/management plants, cruise terminal/ fishing harbors construction and modernization, ecotourism and other livelihoods related infrastructure.

  

* Assessing the proposed infrastructure investments by the client’s teams and providing guidance on: i) spatial targeting or grouping of the proposed investments; ii) assessing any environmental and social (E&S) risks to be considered and propose alternative technical design to mitigate those risks; iii) recommendations to enhance design to be consistent with overall conceptual framework of the project; iv) assessing technical designs to ensure sustainability and resilience of proposed infrastructure; v) ensuring that technical refinements agreed with the Bank’s team are duly included in the teams’ proposals and designs;

  

* Support the task teams in contributing to the preparation of TORs for studies and technical specifications; reviewing the detailed project reports (DPRs); provide Inputs to the draft reports which are to contribute to the project sub-component designs, and; provide guidance on hydrodynamic, climate change and sediment transport modeling intended for a better understanding of the functioning of the coastline and coastal risks,

  

* Provide assistance to the task team and the clients in advising on contract management such as quality control and ensure consultants’ compliance with contracts for engineering design, works supervision, investments operation and maintenance.

  

* Make site visits with other project officers to project intervention sites to review quality of civil works, material results and monthly progress reports, as well as make recommendations for the project on the overall achievement of the projects’ project and quality of works.

  

* Preparation and conduct of supervision missions from technical and financial partners as well as the monitoring of action plans resulting from said missions;

  

* Engage and collaborate with project stakeholders including beneficiaries for knowledge and skills transfer, relating to the prevention and management of coastal risks;

  

* Provide other inputs as requested and agreed with the Bank team.

**Selection Criteria**

* A master’s degree or its equivalent in coastal engineering discipline or civil/hydraulic engineering, specializing in maritime and/or coastal works, dredging, port works, jetties and large-scale mining of rock for breakwaters.

  

* Have at least 5 years of experience in the field of coastal and maritime engineering or coastal oceanography

  

* Have at least three (03) references in studies including the design of coastal protection works or maritime works;

  

* Have at least five (05) experiences in the control and monitoring of coastal or maritime protection works;

  

* Demonstrate knowledge in the specific associated fields such as: climate change, hydrology and coastal oceanography, marine environment, hydrodynamics, morphodynamics of coastal zones, digital

modeling, measurements, design and construction of port and maritime works, sedimentology, upkeep and maintenance maritime works;  
  

* Have a good knowledge of the following common and more specialized software for monitoring and modeling coastal or maritime dynamics will be an added advantage

  

* Have a good knowledge of the environmental and social safeguard measures of the World Bank

  

* Experience working on South Asia and familiarity with the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification framework and ICZM principles in the Indian context is an advantage.

  

* Good team player who can work as a member of a multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural team, motivate and lead group efforts and network effectively across boundaries.

  

* A drive for results while working with limited supervision and under tight timelines.

  
**Additional Considerations:**  
  
As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who:  

* Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries.
* Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making.
* Bring experience working on fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV)-related contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable.

**WBG Culture Attributes:**

1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders.  
2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact.  
3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results.
